summary: The starter prompt clearly defines the core goal: a Node.js Mongoose multi-tenant sample that stores Products, Orders and Inventory in shared Azure DocumentDB collections with tenantId-based isolation and the two compound indexes. The run-time constraints and environment (database name, DOCUMENTDB_URI env var, Node 24 availability, and requirement to verify against the live cluster) are provided in the supplied skill_md. Several implementation choices (exact Mongoose/driver versions, API surface, test strategy, seed script behavior, README contents, and some non-goal constraints) are left to the builder and will be filled by skill guidance or reasonable defaults.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js Mongoose app that stores all merchant products, orders, and inventory in shared DocumentDB collections... enforce tenant isolation at the repository layer"
rubric.note: Business problem and demonstration are explicit: multi-tenant SaaS data isolation in Azure DocumentDB.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Treat as a single-agent coding task / local developer sample (no multi-agent orchestration). The builder will produce a simple repo with scripts and maybe an express API.
rubric.note: Prompt does not mention an agent framework or orchestration; this doesn't block building the sample.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Node.js" (skill_md: "Node.js 24 with npm and npx is available")
rubric.note: Node.js 24 is stated in the provided run environment.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use a modern stable Mongoose (e.g., Mongoose 7.x) compatible with Node 24 and MongoDB 7.0; rely on Mongoose-maintained mongodb driver dependency.
rubric.note: Prompt requires Mongoose but doesn't pin a version; documentdb-driver skill covers driver best practices, not exact package version.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Uses Azure DocumentDB; skill_md: "vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol...)"
rubric.note: Run environment explicitly supplies the cluster type/tier and database name to use.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt silent; skill_md: "connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI. Read it from the environment at run time. Never write its value into any file, log, README or test fixture; use a config file or .env.example with a placeholder"
rubric.note: How to obtain and store the connection string is specified by the run environment guidance.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "stores all merchant products, orders, and inventory in shared DocumentDB collections. Use a tenantId field on every document, include sku on Product and Inventory, and createdAt timestamps" (prompt + skill_md provides DB name sample_retail_10)
rubric.note: Prompt and run environment give the main schema constraints; finer-grain fields are left to implementation.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will add a small seed script with a few tenants, products, inventory rows and orders for demonstration; seed script will be idempotent (upsert by unique key).
rubric.note: Prompt doesn't say what sample data to use or its size/licence or how to load it.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "create compound indexes on (tenantId, sku) and (tenantId, createdAt)" and "enforce tenant isolation at the repository layer"
rubric.note: Index shapes are explicitly requested; documentdb-indexing skill can advise on index choice and creation best practices.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt requests a Node.js Mongoose app and repository layer but does not specify API vs CLI vs UI.
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will provide a minimal Express REST API exposing repository operations (CRUD endpoints) plus npm scripts and a seed script. Business logic will depend only on repository APIs, not direct model usage.
rubric.note: Which endpoints/CLI commands to expose is left to the implementer; this affects examples and tests but not core repo code.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt silent; skill_md: "This sample is being built on a developer machine where an Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned and reachable... Do not provision another cluster unless the run policy says Azure writes are allowed; the cluster above is the one to use."
rubric.note: The run environment forbids creating a new cluster; builder will create collections/indexes on the provided cluster only.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Include README and npm scripts (npm run start, npm run seed, npm test). Tests: at least one integration test that runs against the live cluster (per skill_md) and unit tests that can run offline/mocked.
rubric.note: Prompt/skills don't provide explicit command list or test harness to run; builder will add conventional scripts.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Accept if: schemas defined with tenantId required, compound indexes created and verified at runtime, repository prevents cross-tenant queries and throws when tenantId omitted, seed script loads sample data, and at least one test demonstrates enforcement of tenant isolation.
rubric.note: Prompt lacks formal acceptance criteria; builder will follow the reference requirements and run-environment directives as the checklist.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Do not provision new Azure resources; keep credentials in env vars and .env.example; avoid cross-database changes. No production HA or CMK setups are required for this sample.
rubric.note: The run environment gives one constraint (pre-provisioned cluster) but other cost/scope constraints are not specified.

rubric.found_in_prompt: Prompt requires repository layer and discourages direct model usage; skill_md: "use a config file or .env.example with a placeholder" and database name sample_retail_10
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use conventional Node layout: src/, src/models, src/repos, src/routes, tests/, README.md, .env.example, package.json with scripts. Expose repository-only API for business logic.
rubric.note: Small repo conventions are implied but not fully enumerated.

contradictions: Prompt requests "Using the DocumentDB skill" but there is no single installed skill named exactly "DocumentDB skill"; many documentdb-* skills are installed (documentdb-driver, documentdb-indexing, etc.). Builder will pick appropriate documentdb-* skills.
questions_for_author: Should the sample expose a REST API (Express) for demonstration, or is a CLI + repository library sufficient? This will change the app surface and example usage in the README.
Do you want the sample to pin Mongoose (and mongodb driver) to specific versions, or is 'latest stable compatible with Node 24 / MongoDB 7.0' acceptable?
Should the project include unit tests that run entirely offline (mocking Mongoose) in addition to the live-cluster verification tests required by the run environment?
requirements_at_risk: Seed script idempotency and data-loading details — prompt/skills do not specify a seed dataset, its size or idempotent behavior; builder must invent this.

Automated test that attempts a query without tenantId and asserts the repository rejects it — prompt asks for tenant isolation but does not require a test; no installed skill mandates creating this test.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — test strategy (mocking or in-memory) is not specified by prompt or skills.

Dependencies pinned in a requirements file — the reference mentions pinned dependencies (requirements.txt) but the prompt is a Node.js project and neither prompt nor skills require explicit pinning policy (package-lock.json will exist though).
Infrastructure-as-code for the cluster — run environment says cluster is pre-provisioned and prompt does not request IaC; reference wants IaC but prompt/skills do not provide it.

README coverage (prereqs, setup, run, clean-up) — prompt doesn't require a README; the run environment says to record what was executed, but a full README is not specified and may be omitted or incomplete.

Vector index dimension & parameter selection and related search behaviors — the prompt does not use vector search, while the reference expects vector index choices if used; this is not addressed by prompt or skills for this sample.
